--- title: "Probability Density Estimation 🏔️" subtitle: "MATH 4750 / MSSC 5750 Computational Statistics" format: revealjs: code-line-numbers: false html-math-method: method: mathjax url: "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js" highlight-style: arrow code-block-bg: true self-contained: false slide-number: c/t incremental: false width: 1800 height: 1000 margin: 0.05 logo: "logo.png" footer: "[mmadoliat.github.io/compstat-s27](https://mmadoliat.github.io/compstat-s27/)" theme: ["simple", "slides.scss"] multiplex: false code-link: true fig-cap-location: bottom fig-align: center transition: none ## fade slide convex concave zoom title-slide-attributes: data-background-image: mu-bg.png data-background-size: stretch data-slide-number: none editor: source execute: freeze: auto echo: true purl: true --- # {visibility="hidden"} \def\bx{\mathbf{x}} \def\by{\mathbf{y}} \def\bz{\mathbf{z}} \def\bu{\mathbf{u}} \def\bv{\mathbf{v}} \def\bw{\mathbf{w}} \def\bX{\mathbf{X}} \def\bY{\mathbf{Y}} \def\bZ{\mathbf{Z}} \def\bU{\mathbf{U}} \def\bV{\mathbf{V}} \def\bW{\mathbf{W}} \def\bI{\mathbf{I}} \def\bH{\mathbf{H}} \def\bS{\mathbf{S}} \def\bD{\mathbf{D}} \def\bbeta{\boldsymbol \beta} \def\btheta{\boldsymbol \theta} \def\bmu{\boldsymbol \mu} \def\bSigma{\boldsymbol \Sigma} \def\bLambda{\boldsymbol \Lambda} \def\beps{\boldsymbol \epsilon} \def\T{\text{T}} \def\E{\mathrm{E}} \def\var{\mathrm{Var}} \def\cov{\mathrm{Cov}} \def\cor{\mathrm{Corr}} \def\se{\mathrm{se}} \def\bias{\mathrm{bias}} \def\mse{\mathrm{MSE}} \def\R{\mathbb{R}} \def\P{\mathrm{P}} \def\iid{\stackrel{\text{iid}}{\sim}} \DeclareMathOperator*{\argmin}{arg\,min} \DeclareMathOperator*{\argmax}{arg\,max} # Probability Density Estimation

Histograms: bin width rules (Sturges, Scott, Freedman-Diaconis)

Frequency polygons and averaged shifted histograms

Kernel density estimation and bandwidth selection

Boundary kernels and reflection

Bivariate and multivariate density estimation

::: notes - Rizzo Chapter 12. Everything is a trade-off between bias (too much smoothing) and variance (too little). ::: ## Density Estimation: The Problem - Given $X_1,\dots,X_n\iid f$ (unknown), estimate $f$ **nonparametrically**, i.e., without assuming a family. - Uses: exploratory analysis (modes, skewness), simulation (smoothed bootstrap), classification, mixture assessment (EM, Ch 14). - Accuracy: $\text{MSE}(\hat f(x)) = \var(\hat f(x)) + \bias^2(\hat f(x))$, integrated: $\text{MISE} = \E\int(\hat f - f)^2$. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} par(mfrow = c(1, 3)) for (h in c(1, 4, 12)) { hist(faithful$waiting, breaks = seq(40, 100, by = h), prob = TRUE, col = "#FFCC00", main = paste("bin width h =", h), xlab = "waiting time (min)") } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/16-density/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## The Histogram as a Density Estimate With bins $[t_k, t_{k+1})$ of width $h$ and counts $\nu_k$: $$ \hat f(x) = \frac{\nu_k}{nh},\qquad t_k\le x < t_{k+1}. $$ - $\bias(\hat f(x)) = O(h)$, $\var(\hat f(x)) = O\big(1/(nh)\big)$ $\Rightarrow$ optimal $h\propto n^{-1/3}$, MISE $= O(n^{-2/3})$. **Three bin-width rules:** | Rule | Bin width / classes | Notes | |------|------|------| | Sturges | $k = 1 + \log_2 n$ classes | R default; oversmooths for large $n$ | | Scott | $\hat h = 3.49\,\hat\sigma\,n^{-1/3}$ | normal reference, MISE-optimal for normal | | Freedman-Diaconis | $\hat h = 2\,\text{IQR}\,n^{-1/3}$ | robust to outliers | ## Examples 12.1 - 12.3: Rules in Action ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4750); x <- rnorm(1000) c(Sturges = nclass.Sturges(x), Scott = nclass.scott(x), FD = nclass.FD(x)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Sturges Scott FD 11 19 25 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} waiting <- faithful$waiting; n <- length(waiting) par(mfrow = c(1, 3)) for (rule in c("Sturges", "Scott", "FD")) { hist(waiting, breaks = rule, prob = TRUE, col = "#88A0C8", main = paste("Old Faithful:", rule), xlab = "") } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/16-density/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Estimating $f(x_0)$ from a Histogram (Example 12.2) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} x0 <- 0.1; set.seed(4750); x <- rnorm(1000) br <- pretty(x, n = nclass.scott(x)); h <- diff(br)[1] k <- findInterval(x0, br) c(fhat = sum(x >= br[k] & x < br[k + 1]) / (length(x) * h), true = dnorm(x0), h = h) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` fhat true h 0.372 0.397 0.500 ``` ::: ::: ## Frequency Polygon (Example 12.4) Linear interpolation of the histogram at the bin midpoints. Bias is $O(h^2)$, optimal $h = 2.15\,\sigma n^{-1/5}$ (normal reference). ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} h <- 2.15 * sd(waiting) * n^(-1/5) br <- seq(min(waiting) - h, max(waiting) + h, by = h) H <- hist(waiting, breaks = br, plot = FALSE) mids <- H$mids; dens <- H$density plot(H, freq = FALSE, col = "gray90", main = "Frequency polygon: Old Faithful waiting times", xlab = "") lines(c(mids[1] - h, mids, mids[length(mids)] + h), c(0, dens, 0), lwd = 3, col = "#003366") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/16-density/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Averaged Shifted Histogram (ASH, Example 12.6) Average $m$ histograms with the same width $h$ whose origins are shifted by $h/m$: equivalent to a finer histogram with **triangular weights**. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ash1 <- function(x, h, m = 20, grid = seq(min(x) - h, max(x) + h, length = 400)) { delta <- h / m rowMeans(sapply(0:(m - 1), function(j) { br <- seq(min(x) - h - j * delta, max(x) + 2 * h, by = h) H <- hist(x, breaks = br, plot = FALSE) H$density[findInterval(grid, br, all.inside = TRUE)] })) } grid <- seq(35, 105, length = 400) plot(grid, ash1(waiting, h = 6, grid = grid), type = "l", lwd = 3, col = "#C0392B", xlab = "waiting", ylab = "density", main = "ASH: h = 6, m = 1 vs m = 20") lines(grid, ash1(waiting, h = 6, m = 1, grid = grid), type = "s", col = "gray50") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/16-density/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: # Kernel Density Estimation ## From Histograms to Kernels The **kernel density estimator** places a smooth bump at each observation: $$ \hat f_h(x) = \frac{1}{nh}\sum_{i=1}^nK\!\left(\frac{x - X_i}{h}\right),\qquad K\ge 0,\ \int K = 1. $$ ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4750); xs <- c(-1.5, -1, .2, .4, 1.8); h <- 0.4 gg <- seq(-3.5, 3.5, length = 400) bumps <- sapply(xs, function(xi) dnorm((gg - xi) / h) / (length(xs) * h)) matplot(gg, bumps, type = "l", lty = 2, col = "gray40", xlab = "x", ylab = "", main = "KDE = sum of bumps") lines(gg, rowSums(bumps), lwd = 3, col = "#003366"); rug(xs, lwd = 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/16-density/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Kernels ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/16-density/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: tip The **choice of kernel matters little**; the **bandwidth $h$** matters a lot. ::: ## Bias, Variance, and the Optimal Bandwidth For a second-order kernel with $\sigma_K^2 = \int t^2K(t)\,dt$ and $R(g) = \int g^2$: $$ \bias(\hat f_h(x))\approx\frac{h^2}{2}\sigma_K^2f''(x),\qquad \var(\hat f_h(x))\approx\frac{f(x)R(K)}{nh} $$ $$ \text{AMISE}(h) = \frac{R(K)}{nh} + \frac{h^4}{4}\sigma_K^4R(f'')\quad\Rightarrow\quad h^* = \left(\frac{R(K)}{\sigma_K^4R(f'')n}\right)^{1/5}\propto n^{-1/5}. $$ - MISE rate $O(n^{-4/5})$: better than the histogram's $O(n^{-2/3})$. - **Normal reference** (Gaussian $K$, normal $f$): $h = 1.06\,\hat\sigma\,n^{-1/5}$; **Silverman's rule** `bw.nrd0`: $h = 0.9\min(\hat\sigma, \text{IQR}/1.34)\,n^{-1/5}$. ## Example 12.7: KDE of Old Faithful Waiting Time ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} par(mfrow = c(1, 3)) for (adj in c(.5, 1, 2)) { d <- density(waiting, adjust = adj) plot(d, main = sprintf("bw = %.2f (adjust = %.1f)", d$bw, adj), lwd = 2, col = "#003366") rug(waiting) } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/16-density/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} c(nrd0 = bw.nrd0(waiting), nrd = bw.nrd(waiting), ucv = bw.ucv(waiting), SJ = bw.SJ(waiting)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` nrd0 nrd ucv SJ 3.988 4.696 2.658 2.504 ``` ::: ::: ## Data-Driven Bandwidths: Cross-Validation Least-squares (unbiased) cross-validation minimizes an unbiased estimate of $\text{ISE} - \int f^2$: $$ \text{UCV}(h) = \int\hat f_h^2 - \frac2n\sum_{i=1}^n\hat f_{h,(-i)}(X_i). $$ ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ucv <- function(h, x) { n <- length(x); d <- outer(x, x, "-") int_f2 <- sum(dnorm(d, sd = sqrt(2) * h)) / n^2 # closed form for the Gaussian kernel loo <- (rowSums(dnorm(d / h)) - dnorm(0)) / ((n - 1) * h) int_f2 - 2 * mean(loo) } hs <- seq(1, 8, length = 60); u <- sapply(hs, ucv, x = waiting) plot(hs, u, type = "l", lwd = 3, xlab = "h", ylab = "UCV(h)"); abline(v = hs[which.min(u)], lty = 2, col = 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/16-density/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} c(our_ucv = hs[which.min(u)], bw.ucv = bw.ucv(waiting)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` our_ucv bw.ucv 2.661 2.658 ``` ::: ::: ::: notes - bw.ucv uses a slightly different (binned) approximation, so values differ a little. bw.SJ (Sheather-Jones plug-in) is generally the recommended choice. ::: ## Example 12.8: KDE of Precipitation Data ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) plot(density(precip, bw = "nrd0"), main = "precip: bw.nrd0", lwd = 2); rug(precip) plot(density(precip, bw = "SJ"), main = "precip: bw.SJ", lwd = 2, col = "#C0392B"); rug(precip) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/16-density/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Example 12.9: Evaluating $\hat f(x)$ at Arbitrary Points ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} d <- density(precip) fhat <- approxfun(d$x, d$y) # linear interpolation of the KDE fhat(c(10, 30, 50)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.01097 0.02110 0.01442 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} integrate(fhat, min(d$x), max(d$x))$value # integrates to (about) 1 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1.001 ``` ::: ::: ## Examples 12.10 - 12.11: Boundaries and the Reflection Technique For $f$ supported on $[0,\infty)$, the KDE puts mass below 0 and **underestimates** $f$ near the boundary. **Reflection:** augment the sample with $-X_i$, estimate, then fold: $\hat f_R(x) = 2\hat f_{\{X,-X\}}(x)$ for $x\ge0$. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4750); x <- rexp(1000, 1) d <- density(x, bw = 0.1, n = 1024) xx <- c(x, -x) g <- density(xx, bw = 0.1, n = 1024) a <- seq(0, 6, .01); ux <- a[a < 3.5] plot(d, xlim = c(-0.5, 3.5), ylim = c(0, 1.1), lwd = 2, main = "Exp(1): ordinary vs reflected KDE") lines(g$x[g$x >= 0], 2 * g$y[g$x >= 0], lwd = 2, col = "#C0392B") lines(ux, dexp(ux), lty = 2, lwd = 2) legend("topright", c("ordinary KDE", "reflection", "true"), col = c(1, "#C0392B", 1), lty = c(1, 1, 2), lwd = 2, bty = "n") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/16-density/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: # Bivariate and Multivariate Density Estimation ## Example 12.12 - 12.13: Bivariate Frequency Table and Density Polygon ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} bin2d <- function(x, breaks1 = "Sturges", breaks2 = "Sturges") { histg1 <- hist(x[, 1], breaks = breaks1, plot = FALSE) histg2 <- hist(x[, 2], breaks = breaks2, plot = FALSE) freq <- table(cut(x[, 1], histg1$breaks), cut(x[, 2], histg2$breaks)) list(call = match.call(), freq = freq, breaks1 = histg1$breaks, breaks2 = histg2$breaks, mids1 = histg1$mids, mids2 = histg2$mids) } b <- bin2d(as.matrix(faithful)) par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) image(b$mids1, b$mids2, unclass(b$freq), col = hcl.colors(20, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE), xlab = "eruptions", ylab = "waiting", main = "2-d frequency table") persp(b$mids1, b$mids2, unclass(b$freq), theta = 30, phi = 30, col = "#FFCC00", shade = .4, xlab = "eruptions", ylab = "waiting", zlab = "count", main = "density polygon") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/16-density/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ## Example 12.15: Product Kernel Estimate $$ \hat f(\bx) = \frac{1}{nh_1\cdots h_d}\sum_{i=1}^n\prod_{j=1}^dK\!\left(\frac{x_j - X_{ij}}{h_j}\right),\qquad h_j\propto\hat\sigma_jn^{-1/(d+4)}. $$ ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4750) n <- 2000; p <- c(.2, .3, .5) mu <- matrix(c(0, 1, 4, 0, 3, -1), 3, 2); Sigma <- diag(2) i <- sample(1:3, replace = TRUE, prob = p, size = n) xbvn <- t(sapply(i, function(k) MASS::mvrnorm(1, mu[k, ], Sigma))) fhat <- MASS::kde2d(xbvn[, 1], xbvn[, 2], n = 60) # Gaussian product kernel, normal-reference bandwidths par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1)) contour(fhat, main = "kde2d: contours"); points(mu, pch = 19, col = 2) persp(fhat, phi = 30, theta = 20, d = 5, xlab = "x", ylab = "y", col = "#88A0C8", border = NA, shade = .5) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](./images/16-density/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: notes - MASS::kde2d uses a Gaussian product kernel with bandwidth.nrd() in each coordinate (it divides h by 4 internally). ks::kde provides full bandwidth matrices and plug-in selectors. ::: ## The Curse of Dimensionality in Density Estimation - Optimal MISE rate for a KDE in $d$ dimensions: $O\big(n^{-4/(4+d)}\big)$. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} d <- c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10) data.frame(d = d, rate = paste0("n^(-", round(4 / (4 + d), 2), ")"), n_needed_for_1d_accuracy_of_n100 = round(100^((4 + d) / 5))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` d rate n_needed_for_1d_accuracy_of_n100 1 1 n^(-0.8) 100 2 2 n^(-0.67) 251 3 3 n^(-0.57) 631 4 5 n^(-0.44) 3981 5 10 n^(-0.29) 398107 ``` ::: ::: - To match the accuracy of $n = 100$ in 1-d, we need enormous samples in 10-d. This is why PCA/dimension reduction (Ch 5) is used before density estimation. ## Python Supplement ```{.python} import numpy as np from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde waiting = np.loadtxt("faithful_waiting.txt") kde = gaussian_kde(waiting, bw_method="silverman") grid = np.linspace(40, 100, 200) dens = kde(grid) ``` ## Summary ::: instructions - Histogram: $h\propto n^{-1/3}$ (Scott, FD); Sturges oversmooths for large $n$. - Frequency polygon and ASH: cheap, bias $O(h^2)$. - KDE: $\hat f = \frac1{nh}\sum K((x - X_i)/h)$; bandwidth is what matters: `bw.nrd0`, `bw.SJ`, cross-validation. - Boundaries need care (reflection); higher dimensions need much more data. :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
